      type: object
      properties:
        type:

          format: uri

          title: Title

          example: NoResourceFoundException

        status:

          description: HTTP status code
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 400
          maximum: 600
          exclusiveMaximum: true
          example: 500
          readOnly: true
        detail:
          title: Detail
          description: The long error message.
          type: string
          example: 'No static resource api/owner.'
          readOnly: true
        timestamp:
          title: Timestamp
          description: The time the error occurred.
          type: string
          format: date-time
          example: '2024-11-23T13:59:21.3820407Z'
          readOnly: true

          title: Schema validation errors
          description: Validation errors against the OpenAPI schema.
          type: array
          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/ValidationMessage'
      required:
        - type
        - title
        - status
        - detail
        - timestamp
        - schemaValidationErrors
    ValidationMessage:
      title: Validation message
      description: Messages describing a validation error.
      type: object
      properties:
        message:
          title: Message
          description: The validation message.
          type: string
          example: "[Path '/lastName'] Instance type (null) does not match any allowed primitive type (allowed: ['string'])"

      required:
        - message

## What I changed

The `sharesHousehold` flag was already handled end-to-end (`RejectDuplicateHousehold` skips the duplicate-address check when it's true). What was missing was the `householdId` field. I added it as a **deterministically derived, read-only response field** rather than a persisted column:

1. **`openapi.yml`** — added a read-only `householdId` property to the `Owner` response schema (so the generated `OwnerDto` exposes it), documented as "shared by every owner with the same last name and address."

2. **`HouseholdId.java`** (new helper in `rest.function.owner`) — `HouseholdId.of(lastName, address)` normalizes last name + address the *same way* as `RejectDuplicateHousehold` (trim, collapse whitespace, lower-case) and returns the first 12 upper-case hex chars of SHA-256 over the pair.

3. **`OwnerMapper.java`** — added a MapStruct `@Mapping` expression that fills `householdId` from the owner's last name and address, mirroring how `displayName`/`initials` are derived.

## Why this design

Because `householdId` is a pure function of `lastName` + `address`, any two owners in the same household (matching last name and address — exactly the owners `sharesHousehold: true` permits) compute the *identical, stable* id automatically, with no cross-owner lookup or mutation of existing rows. That satisfies "assign both the same householdId (a stable shared identifier)" while avoiding a schema migration, entity field, `data.sql` seed edits, and a new pipeline step — a smaller, lower-risk change than persisting the column (following the pattern of `displayName`/`initials`, not `customerCode` which needs persistence because it uses a global sequence).

The test creates owner `a`, then `b` and `c` with `a`'s last name/address and `sharesHousehold: true`; it asserts `b` and `c` return equal, non-blank `householdId` values via `GET /api/owners/{id}` — which now holds.
